title: The Coxeter-Diagram Side of the Platonic Correspondence
content: The parent entry identified each Platonic solid's reflection group by its degrees (A₃=⟨2,3,4⟩, B₃=⟨2,4,6⟩, H₃=⟨2,6,10⟩). This follow-up uses the *other* canonical datum — the Coxeter diagram. A regular polyhedron {p,q} is the linear rank-3 Coxeter group with diagram o–p–o–q–o (Coxeter matrix m₁₂=p, m₂₃=q, m₁₃=2). From the pair (p,q) alone we recover the group, its order via the direct Schläfli formula 8pq/(2p+2q−pq), and its finiteness via the spherical criterion pq<2p+2q.
mathContext: The Coxeter matrix of {p,q} comes from the characteristic triangle with angles π/p, π/q, π/2; the diagram is a path, so the group is encoded by the bond pair (p,q).

title: CoxDiagram: the Linear Rank-3 Diagram
content: `CoxDiagram` stores the two bond labels a=m₁₂ and b=m₂₃ of a path diagram o–a–o–b–o; the outer bond m₁₃=2 (end nodes commute) is implicit and recorded by `outerBond`. `diagram s = ⟨p,q⟩` reads the labels off the Schläfli symbol, and `diagA₃=⟨3,3⟩`, `diagB₃=⟨4,3⟩`, `diagH₃=⟨5,3⟩` are the three canonical diagrams.
mathContext: That the outer bond is 2 (the two non-adjacent mirrors are perpendicular) is exactly what makes the rank-3 diagram a path rather than a triangle — the defining feature of the [p,q] family.

title: Diagrams of the Five Solids
content: `diagram_values` and `canonical_diagrams`: the five solids have diagrams ⟨3,3⟩, ⟨4,3⟩, ⟨3,4⟩, ⟨5,3⟩, ⟨3,5⟩, and the tetrahedron/cube/dodecahedron realize the canonical A₃=[3,3], B₃=[4,3], H₃=[5,3]. Each is `rfl` — the diagram is definitionally the Schläfli pair.
mathContext: Cube ⟨4,3⟩ and octahedron ⟨3,4⟩ are mirror-image diagrams; dodecahedron ⟨5,3⟩ and icosahedron ⟨3,5⟩ likewise — foreshadowing that duality is reversal.

title: Duality is Diagram Reversal
content: `reverse ⟨a,b⟩ = ⟨b,a⟩` reads the path from the other end (an involution, `reverse_reverse`). `dual_reverses_diagram` proves diagram(dual s) = reverse(diagram s): Platonic duality p↔q reflects the diagram about its centre. `normalize` sorts the bonds (min,max); `normalize_reverse` shows reversal leaves the normalised diagram fixed (via min/max commutativity), so the sorted diagram is a reversal-invariant signature of the path.
mathContext: Reversing a Coxeter diagram gives an isomorphic Coxeter group; hence dual solids, whose diagrams are reverses, must share their reflection group.

title: Normalised Diagram Determines the Group
content: `normalize_determines_coxeter`: across the five solids, equal normalised diagrams force equal reflection groups (a 5×5 `decide` case split). Composed with `dual_normalize_diagram` it yields `coxeter (dual s) = coxeter s` (`coxeter_dual_via_diagram`) — the parent proved this from the degrees; here it falls out purely from the diagram. This is the structural reason five solids give only three groups: their diagrams form three reversal classes {[3,3]}, {[4,3],[3,4]}, {[5,3],[3,5]}.
mathContext: The map (normalised diagram) ↦ (reflection group) is well-defined and injective on the three classes that occur, so counting groups reduces to counting reversal classes of diagrams.

title: The Direct Schläfli Order Formula
content: `defect s = 2p+2q−pq` (values 3,2,2,1,1) is the angular-defect denominator. `order_from_schlafli` proves |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq) equals the parent's group order, and `schlafli_order_eq_four_edges` shows it equals 4E — all by `decide`, the ℕ-division being exact for each solid. So the order is computed straight from {p,q}: e.g. dodecahedron 8·15/(10+6−15)=120/1=120.
mathContext: This is the classical order g of the spherical group [p,q]; equivalently 4/(1/p+1/q−1/2). It reproduces both 4E and the product-of-degrees without invoking any group structure.

title: The Spherical (Finiteness) Criterion
content: `isSpherical p q := pq < 2p+2q` is the Schläfli inequality 1/p+1/q>1/2 cleared of denominators. `solids_spherical` shows all five solids satisfy it; `euclidean_boundary_not_spherical` shows the three regular Euclidean tilings {3,6},{4,4},{6,3} do not (they have defect 0); `spherical_iff_defect_pos` ties sphericity to a positive defect, i.e. to the order formula being defined.
mathContext: The trichotomy 1/p+1/q > = < 1/2 separates the finite (spherical/Platonic) groups from the infinite Euclidean and hyperbolic ones. The Platonic solids are exactly the strict interior; the three tilings sit on the boundary.

title: Capstone: Diagram + Order + Duality
content: `schlafli_coxeter_correspondence` bundles the whole story per solid: diagram s = ⟨p,q⟩; |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq) = 4E; the solid is spherical; and duality reverses the diagram while preserving the group. This is the diagram-side analogue of the parent's invariant-level capstone.
mathContext: A single statement certifying that the Coxeter-diagram datum, the Schläfli order formula, sphericity, and duality-as-reversal all hold simultaneously for each of the five Platonic solids.
